newsitem.title: UK: BG receives $134 mln in J-block settlement.
newsitem.headline: BG receives $134 mln in J-block settlement.

text.p: BG Plc said it received $134.2 million in cash as part of a total $440 million payment by Enron Corp in settlement of contractual issues with BG and its partners in the North Sea gas producing J-block.
BG and its J-block partners Phillips UK and Agip produced from the J-block under a long-term "take-or-pay contract".
But because of a slump in prices on the U.K. spot market, Enron would not take delivery of gas before September 30, 1998.
Enron also did not agree a commissioning date, so seeking to defer the start of its take-or-pay obligations.
As part of the settlement, the fixed contract price Enron will have to pay is cut "...to reflect current market conditions for long-term gas sales contracts," BG said.
But Enron will continue to buy essentially the same amounts of gas as under the previous supply agreement, it added.
"The settlement concludes all J-block litigation with Enron," David Varney, chief executive of BG said in a statement.
BG said it expected J-block gross production starting from July and for the rest of 1997 to average 260 million cubic feet of gas per day.
Initial gas sales will start in June at lesser volumes.
